sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Now the per-action breakdown is clear:
1. RIGHT: pink 64, no change to the timer.
2. SPACE: pink 64→63. So SPACE consumes 1.
3. UP: pink 63, no change.
4. UP: pink 63, no change.
5. UP: pink 63→62! And the player moved from rows 40-43 to rows 36-39. Wait — the 5th transition is UP, and the player moved to rows 36-39, and pink decreased to 62. Hmm, interesting. So this UP consumed 1 from the timer. Why? Maybe the player's movement got blocked? No, the player moved. Or... the player's white edge (facing up) touched something? At rows 36-39, the player's top edge is row 36. The nose frame is at rows 36-39, cols 32-35 — not adjacent (player is cols 36-39, nose is cols 32-35, adjacent horizontally at the col 35/36 boundary). Hmm.
Wait, let me actually reconsider: maybe the timer decreases when the player moves into a position adjacent to a frame? Or when the player's facing edge touches an object?
6. LEFT: pink 62, no change, the nose frame broke (nose_frame 0), the player stayed at cols 36-39 (blocked by the frame).
So the timer decreased on SPACE and on the 5th UP. What's special about that UP? The player moved to rows 36-39, cols 36-39. The nose frame is at rows 36-39, cols 32-35 — now the player is directly adjacent (sharing an edge at col 35|36). Hmm, but the LEFT after that (the collision) didn't decrease it.
Or maybe the timer decreases when the player becomes adjacent to an object? Or when the player's movement is "blocked" in the facing direction? The 5th UP: the player moved from rows 40-43 to 36-39 — it moved, wasn't blocked.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the pink bar isn't a timer at all — maybe it's a "health" that decreases when you touch something? The 5th UP placed the player adjacent to the nose frame (edge-to-edge contact at col 35/36, rows 36-39). And SPACE... the player was at rows 48-51, cols 36-39, facing right. What was adjacent? Nothing. Hmm.
Or maybe the pink bar decreases with each "action" but with some delay? Sequence: actions 1-6: RIGHT, SPACE, UP, UP, UP, LEFT. Pink: 64, 63, 63, 63, 62, 62. Decreases at action 2 (SPACE) and action 5 (UP). Hmm, every 3 actions? 2 and 5... next would be 8? That's odd.
Maybe it decreases when the player's facing edge touches an object or the boundary? SPACE: player facing right at cols 36-39... nothing at col 40. Hmm, no.
Let me think from a different angle. Maybe the pink bar is a countdown that decreases every N steps regardless of action (a real-time timer?). The run_elapsed_seconds is increasing. Maybe the pink bar decreases in real time (like 1 per 30 seconds)? At the time of the SPACE action, elapsed was 129.87 seconds. At the time of the 5th UP... I don't know the exact elapsed. Hmm, the first action was at elapsed 77 seconds, the second at 129.9 seconds. If the bar decreases in real time, it should have decreased at some point.
Actually, wait: maybe the pink bar is a countdown of remaining "moves" that decreases per action, but the display is... no, RIGHT didn't decrease it.
Let me test: perform a few more moves and observe the pink. For example, RIGHT (moving away from the nose), then check pink. Also test whether the timer decreases on collision.
Actually, more importantly: what's the goal? The nose frame broke when the player collided with it from the right (LEFT move). The blue core remained. Maybe the goal is to break all the charcoal frames (3 of them: 2 eyes + nose)? Or to collect the blue cores?
Wait — maybe the goal is to "eat" the blue 2×2 cores. When the player collided with the nose frame, the frame broke but the blue core remained. Maybe if you collide with the blue core directly, you eat it?
Or maybe the game is: the face is a monster, and you have to break its parts? The pink bar = monster's health? Hmm.
Let me look at the image again: the face now has 2 eyes (charcoal frames with blue), a mouth (blue with gray), and the nose is just a blue square on the background (frame gone). The player is green with a white left edge, right next to the nose's blue core.
Hypothesis: the goal is to collect all the blue 2×2 cores (the "gems") by bumping into them. The charcoal frames are protective shells that break on collision. After breaking the nose's shell, the player needs to bump into the blue core to collect it.
Test: press LEFT again — the player should collide with the blue core at cols 33-34 (rows 37-38). If the blue core disappears and the score increases, the hypothesis is confirmed.

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content:
World model: Timer decreases on SPACE and on the 5th UP (unclear rule — possibly real-time or contact-based). The nose's charcoal frame broke when the player bumped into it. The blue 2×2 core remains. Hypothesis: bumping breaks the shell. Bumping into the blue core collects it (goal = collect all blue cores).
Plan: Press LEFT to bump into the nose's blue core and check for collection/score.

print("pink:", [n['pixels'] for n in a if n['color']=='P'])
